name: Ethical Purchasing Group - SIA Project 22 23
description:
Information Systems – 2022/2023
Course Project
Consider the following scenario:

A km-zero fruit and vegetable store wants to develop a management system for am Ethical Purchasing Group (EPS; in Italian, Gruppo di Acquisti Solidale, or GAS) that connects a number of customers (family groups or generally groups of people) and some farmers. The basic philosophy is a conscious approach to purchasing, involving knowledge of the origin, quality, and different types of products.

The supporting information system should provide service to customers, farmers, and store employees.

The operating cycle of the EPS is weekly:
- Starting at 12 noon on Friday and by 9 a.m. on Saturday morning, farmers provide an estimate of available products, in terms of types, prices, and quantities,
- Customer orders are accepted until 11 p.m. on Sunday,
- By 9 a.m. on Monday morning the farmers confirm the availability of products,
- At this point the system automatically performs payments from customers' virtual wallets,
- After payment has been made, customers can schedule times to pick up produce,
- By Tuesday evening, farmers deliver their products to the store,
- Pickups can take place from Wednesday morning to Friday evening.

The information system has a catalog of products that describes the characteristics, contains photos, and indicates the unit of measurement with which they are sold (for example: €/kg). In addition, a minimum and a maximum quantity that can be ordered is indicated.

The availabilities entered by farmers refer to a product in the catalog, specify the total quantity available and a price (with the same unit of measure indicated in the catalog). It is also possible to indicate crop characteristics, e.g., small size, excellent quality, very ripe, etc.

Customers can choose from all the offerings of the various farmers by specifying the quantity and completing an order. The order can be placed directly by customers via the web or by store employees at the customers' request. Once the customer confirms the product entry, the system verifies that the minimum quantities are met: if not, the customer must modify the order before it can be finally confirmed. Once the order is completed, a summary email is sent to the customer.

Please note that the customer is a representative of a buying group, typically family groups or more generally groups of people. Therefore, only the group representative can enter group orders into the system.

Customer orders are in the "entered" state until the farmers confirm available quantities. If the available quantities are sufficient to cover the orders, the orders move to the "confirmed" status. If there is no availability for all orders of a certain product, according to the system's precedence rules, unavailable quantities are removed from lower precedence orders. Modified orders go into the "modified" status and must be viewed and accepted by customers. If all products in an order are unavailable, then the order is cancelled. Upon delivery of the farmers' products, the clerk confirms receipt of the products in the specified quantity. If by 4 p.m. on Tuesday the goods have still not been delivered the system sends a reminder via SMS. If at the end of the day (8 p.m.) the goods have not been delivered, the system changes the orders related to delivery, re-credits the amount of goods not present with a bonus of 20% and reports the inconvenience to customers.

Payment of orders is made after confirmation of quantities by farmers, for the quantities actually in the order. Payment is made from a personal wallet that users can top up at any time through the store.

After order placement, if the customer's wallet balance is insufficient, a warning is sent via email but the order is still accepted.

If the balance is insufficient at the time of payment, a message (SMS) is sent to the customer who has until Monday evening to top up their wallet. If the balance is not sufficient on Monday evening, the order is cancelled.

As soon as the payment is made (automatically by the system) customers can book an appointment to pick up their products at the store.

Store employees at the beginning of their shift view the pickup schedule and prepare packages for customers, when they arrive they register the pickup of products.

In case of failure to pick up on time, the system sends an SMS alert to the customer.

If the customer has not picked up their order by Friday, it is marked as "forfeited" and the customer's fair play score is updated as detailed in the following.

The system has a mean of evaluation the “fair play” of customers registered in the system. The customer’s fair play score is a measure of how correctly the users behave regarding their orders. This score is maintained in the system and is used as a mean of precedence in case of limited availability of produce. The “fair play” score is computed based on four different indicators: O) number of computed orders; R) number of reminders received; F) number of forfeited pickups; M) number of modified orders. When there is not enough availability of produce for all orders, the customers with higher score are given precedence over those with lower score.
highLevelGoals: Customers want to easily browse available products from various farmers and place orders for their buying group.
Customers need to be able to top up their virtual wallet and have payments for confirmed orders processed automatically.
Customers desire the flexibility to schedule a suitable time to pick up their ordered produce from the store.
Customers expect to be informed about their order status, including confirmations, modifications, and payment issues.
Customers aim to behave responsibly with their orders and pickups to ensure higher precedence in case of limited product availability.
Farmers need to submit estimates of available products, including types, prices, and quantities, within the specified timeframe.
Farmers must confirm the actual availability of products to fulfill customer orders by the deadline.
Farmers are responsible for delivering their confirmed products to the store by Tuesday evening.
Store employees should be able to place orders on behalf of customers when requested.
Store employees need to verify and confirm the receipt of products from farmers, ensuring quantities match.
Store employees must view the pickup schedule and prepare packages for customers before their arrival.
Store employees need to record when customers pick up their ordered products.
lowLevelGoals: The customer can view a list of all products currently available for order, including details like product name, farmer, price, and estimated quantity.
The customer can filter the displayed product list to show only products from a specific farmer.
The customer can filter the displayed product list to show only products of a specific type (e.g., vegetables, fruits).
The customer can select a product and specify the desired quantity to add it to their shopping cart.
The customer can remove a previously added product from their shopping cart.
The customer can modify the quantity of a product already in their shopping cart.
The customer can view a summary of all products in their shopping cart, including quantities and total estimated cost.
The customer can submit their shopping cart as a new order.
The system automatically verifies that all products in a customer's order meet the specified minimum quantity requirements.
The customer can check their current virtual wallet balance.
The customer can start the process of adding funds to their virtual wallet.
The customer can specify the amount of money they wish to add to their virtual wallet.
The customer can confirm the top-up transaction after selecting the amount and payment method.
The system automatically deducts the total cost of a confirmed order from the customer's virtual wallet.
The system automatically sends an SMS notification to the customer if their virtual wallet balance is insufficient to cover a confirmed order.
The system automatically cancels a customer's order if the virtual wallet is not topped up by Monday evening after an insufficient balance notification.
The customer can view a list of available time slots for picking up their order.
The customer can choose a specific date and time from the available pickup slots for their order.
The customer can confirm their selected pickup time slot for an order.
The system automatically sends an SMS alert to the customer if they fail to pick up their order within the scheduled time.
The customer can check the current status of their placed orders (e.g., pending, confirmed, ready for pickup, picked up).
The system sends an automatic notification to the customer when their order is confirmed by the farmers.
The system sends an automatic notification to the customer if their order is modified (e.g., due to product unavailability).
The customer can view and accept a modified order after receiving a modification notification.
The system sends an automatic notification to the customer if there is an issue with processing payment for their order.
The customer can view their current fair play score.
The system automatically updates a customer's fair play score based on their order and pickup behavior, including orders, reminders, forfeits, and modifications.
The farmer can input and submit their estimated product availability, including product type, price per unit, and quantity, for a specific ordering cycle.
The farmer can edit previously submitted product estimates before the submission deadline.
The farmer can view a list of customer orders that require their confirmation based on actual product availability.
For each item in a pending order, the farmer can confirm the exact quantity they can supply.
The system automatically confirms a customer's order based on farmer availability confirmations and applies precedence rules.
The system automatically modifies a customer's order if the confirmed product quantity from farmers is less than ordered, applying precedence rules.
The system automatically cancels a customer's order if products are entirely unavailable after farmer confirmation and precedence rules.
The farmer can view their confirmed delivery schedule, including a list of products and quantities to be delivered to the store.
The system automatically sends an SMS reminder to a farmer if their delivery is not confirmed by the store employee by 4 p.m. on Tuesday.
The store employee can create and submit an order on behalf of a customer, selecting products and quantities.
The store employee can view a list of expected product deliveries from farmers, including product details and quantities.
The store employee can mark individual products from a farmer's delivery as received, specifying the actual quantity.
The system automatically re-credits customer virtual wallets for products not delivered by farmers by the deadline.
The system automatically logs and reports instances of farmer non-delivery or late delivery.
The store employee can view a schedule of customer pickups, including customer names, order details, and scheduled times.
The store employee can mark a customer's order as prepared and ready for pickup.
The store employee can search for a specific customer's order using criteria like customer name or order ID.
The store employee can mark a customer's order as successfully picked up.
